messages.content: What are the components of Civil Law?

message.content:
Civil law is a broad legal system that governs non-criminal disputes between private parties. Its components can be grouped into several key categories: | Category | What it Covers | Typical Examples | |----------|----------------|------------------| | **Sources of Law** | The foundations from which civil law derives its authority. | • Statutes (legislated rules)
• Regulations (executive rules)
• Case law (judicial decisions)
• Customary law (long‑standing practices) | | **Legal Principles** | Core doctrines that shape how civil law is interpreted and applied. | • *Respondeat superior* (employer liability)
• *Caveat emptor* (buyer beware)
• *Stare decisis* (precedent) | | **Areas of Law** | Specific subject matters within civil law. | • Contract law
• Tort law
• Property law
• Family law
• Corporate law
• Succession (inheritance) | | **Procedural Rules** | How civil cases are conducted in court. | • Pleadings (complaints, answers)
• Discovery (information exchange)
• Trial procedures
• Appeals | | **Remedies** | Outcomes or reliefs available to parties. | • Damages (compensatory, punitive)
• Injunctions (orders to do or stop doing something)
• Declaratory judgments (clarifying rights) | | **Institutions** | Bodies that enforce civil law. | • Civil courts (trial, appellate)
• Arbitration panels
• Mediation services | | **Legal Processes** | Steps taken to resolve disputes. | • Negotiation
• Mediation
• Arbitration
• Litigation | | **Legal Professionals** | People who practice civil law. | • Attorneys (lawyers)
• Judges
• Paralegals
• Legal clerks | | **Legal Documents** | Written instruments used in civil law. | • Contracts
• Deeds
• Wills
• Court filings | These components interact to form a comprehensive framework that governs relationships, obligations, and rights among private individuals and entities.
